_about: Register of the third-party data lists shipped in the extension: where each comes from, which tool rebuilds it, and the extension version (major.minor) it was last rebuilt for. updateOn "minor" = rebuild once per minor release (4.2 → 4.3), never required for a patch (4.3.1 → 4.3.2). Enforced by check-list-freshness.mjs (complete-check step list-freshness). Updated by each list's tool — do not edit by hand except to add a list. 4.5.4: EVERY shipped list file (data/spam-tlds.js and every lib/downloadsentinel/util/*.default.js) must be registered here and rebuilt by a tool in this package — check-list-freshness.mjs fails on an unregistered list. Lists without updateOn are curated (rebuilt when their source is edited). sameSnapshotAs: two lists built from one raw snapshot must record the same sourceRelease.

top-sites.what: Chrome UX Report origins ranked ≤ 100,000 → registered domains, + brand websites + GovSuffixes (gen-brands-data.mjs) → Bloom filter (look-alike check; DownloadSentinel 3.2.0 method since 4.3.0)
top-sites.licence: CC BY 4.0 — Chrome UX Report by Google

platform-suffixes.what: Public Suffix List PRIVATE section — platforms where anyone gets a subdomain (no domain age for those sites)

rdap-cctlds.what: Two-letter ccTLDs with an RDAP service (IANA RDAP bootstrap) — others have no domain age

abused-tlds.what: HaGeZi 'The World's Most Abused TLDs' — 3P scripts/frames blocked from level 2 up; first-party visit = heuristics signal only (core/site-scorer.js SPAM_TLDS check)
abused-tlds._note: Added to this register in the 4.5.1 audit (was shipped but unregistered since first introduced — C39a gap). Rebuilt with build-spam-tlds.mjs (from the already-cached spam-tlds-ublock.txt — same 445 TLDs / 1039 exceptions, source release unchanged) to confirm the register and the shipped file actually match, not just to bump the version stamp.

host-list.what: Merged, deduplicated host-risk table: HaGeZi DynDNS + HaGeZi Badware Hoster + Kees1958 'Suspicious websites' (risk score only, never a block — feeds core/site-scorer.js's site-visit check AND core/download-guard.js's download check via BrowserProtection.js/ScoringEngineV2.js). Kees1958's entries here are a SEPARATE snapshot from data/suspicious-hosting.js's own Kees1958 ingestion (that one is a hard block, protection 6) — see each file's header; this register entry does not cover data/suspicious-hosting.js, which carries no update tool of its own in this project's tools artifact (see README/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES for that gap).
host-list.licence: GPLv3 — HaGeZi DNS blocklists; Kees1958 repository has no LICENSE file on file (confirmed 2026-10-21)
host-list._note: Added to this register in the 4.5.1 audit (C39a gap — this list was shipped, consumed by two separate check paths, but had no register entry, and the only script that rebuilt it was DownloadSentinel's own update-lists.mjs, which hardcodes an EXT_ROOT = REPO_ROOT/EXTENSION sibling-folder layout matching neither the DS tools artifact nor this project's actual lib/downloadsentinel/{util,...} tree). Closed in the same audit by rebuild-host-list.mjs — a native 3P-Matrix-tools script that ports the identical merge logic (same sources, same scores, same overlap exclusion against this extension's own SuspiciousDomains.js/RiskyHostingSites.js) against this project's own file paths, per the user's 'don't touch DS' instruction. Rebuilt result: still 2642 domains (was 2642) — same data, now actually produced by a tool this project owns.

public-suffix-list.what: Public Suffix List — registrable-domain boundaries (site, download and look-alike checks); same snapshot as platform-suffixes

brands.what: Brand keyword → real websites (look-alike + brand-impersonation checks)

gov-suffixes.what: Shared government suffixes — real sites, never a brand; unioned into top-sites

suspicious-domains.what: Risk scores for domains frequently used in malware delivery

risky-hosting-sites.what: User-upload / file-sharing platforms with a risk score
